summary:
# NOTES: THE O'RUDDY (Crane & Barr, 1903; single book, first-person narrator Tom O'Ruddy)

## Ch I-II (Bristol)
- Narrator Tom O'Ruddy, of Glandore near Old Head of Kinsale; age 18 at father's death. Father's last words: "I brought you into existence, and God help you safe out of it." Money lasts 5 years. Ship "Martha Bixby" out of Bristol.
- Legacy: two swords (grand one from King Louis; plain one), cask of brandy, papers belonging to young Lord Strepp (now Earl of Westport, London). Father lent Strepp breeches in French campaign. Advice: "never be civil to a king's officer... red coat."
- Steward Mickey Clancy; Father Donovan (priest).
- Bristol inn: fat landlord; O'Ruddy's civil speech mistaken for roguery.
- Supper: garrulous man in plum-colour; Lord Strepp (~20, fair unpowdered hair); Colonel Clarence Royale (~40, clear-eyed); Reginald Forister (dark-skinned, proud). Strepp reluctant to tell breeches story. O'Ruddy: "That, sir, is a lie." Gives lie twice.
- Strepp visits: Royale wants a duel. O'Ruddy claims a friend will attend (lie). Strepp: "I am The O'Ruddy."
- Forister mocks Irish ("naked... clubs"); O'Ruddy boxes his ear, kicks him through front door into inn yard; Forister crashes into servant with cloaks/cushions.
- Earl of Westport (tall, "like an old eagle") with two ladies and a bargeman with a cold. Earl: "Rubbish!" then "Come to my chamber in the morning, O'Ruddy." Pair of bright eyes glimpsed in a hood (Mary).
- Strepp and Royale seen laughing under taproom window.

## Ch II (duel, Paddy)
- O'Ruddy meets Irish keening vagrant Paddy (huge red hair, blue eyes, Irish). Dresses him in father's blue velvet, flowered waistcoat, pink stockings, cocked hat, cloak. Sword on string from neck.
- Paddy's "lashings" (custom of his country) confuses Strepp.
- Duel on green turf. O'Ruddy laughs in Royale's face; Royale enraged, wounded four times; Strepp stops it. Royale: "I couldn't reach him."
- O'Ruddy: "Well, I won't kill him." Crowd of boys; Paddy dubbed "King of Ireland."

## Ch III-IV (papers, Jem Bottles)
- Papers stolen. Paddy has them (one badly worn at heel). O'Ruddy suspects Forister.
- Bristol landlord: Forister took horse for Bath.
- Highwayman Jem Bottles (mother Dame Bottles; ballads: seven in Bristol, three in Bath; sheep-stealer turned highwayman; Farmer Hants, Susan, eggs). Bottles robbed O'Ruddy. Hidden horses behind mother's cottage. Dame Bottles and her plum-stew, cheese, snuff-boxes.
- O'Ruddy borrows Jem's 14 guineas (total 15; O'Ruddy 1 guinea).
- Bath inn: Forister gone back to Bristol.
- Wayside inn near Bristol: Jem's sweetheart (chambermaid); Paddy has barricaded Forister in a room ("little black devil", "little black man").

## Ch V-VI (Forister, Earl, Mary)
- Forister: "king of the Irelands"; denies papers ("I have not your foolish papers"). Threatens to kill O'Ruddy in Bristol.
- Bristol inn: Strepp and Royale warm. Earl's valet Tompkins. Earl in bed: "Worthless! Straw! Nothing but straw!" Accuses O'Ruddy of plot to ruin him. Earl coughing blood into napkin.
- Lady Mary enters ("Come, Mary... Ruffle my pillows"). O'Ruddy's scabbard tinkles; he "stood like a stone."
- Earl: "keep stern watch of your jewels." O'Ruddy: "You yourself stole my papers!"
- Packet falls from Earl's pillows; O'Ruddy snatches it. Swords drawn; O'Ruddy flings his sword down hilt-first, gives papers to Mary.
- Royale: "I would stake my life that you are in the right." Strepp: Forister is his father's partner in shipping; Mary fond of him.
- Royale: Forister's wrist "reminds one of a top." O'Ruddy resolves to run away.

## Ch VII-IX (Forister, parrot, duel)
- O'Ruddy considers return to Ireland. Forister visits: "I have decided to kill you." Mention of "Nell" (Bristol girl) and "the child." O'Ruddy's taunts.
- Strepp and Royale formal and comic (door ceremony).
- Garden: Countess and Mary; parrot "Pretty lady!"; Countess: "I cannot endure parrots." Parrot: "Old harridan!"
- Mary speaks to O'Ruddy: "don't fight with Forister... 'Tis certain death." He takes offence; she: "Proceed now, sir, in your glowing stupidity."
- Next morning: Royale carries note from Mary: "God spare you!" (O'Ruddy and Forister each receive one.) Royale's jealousy: he has watched Mary since babyhood.
- Duel: O'Ruddy's rage and fast attack. Forister's left shoulder pierced; Forister flings sword; Strepp stops it. Royale: "You are great!"

## Ch X-XII (chairs, Countess, robbery, Bath)
- O'Ruddy famous; servants flee. Coffee-room chair farce. Countess (Hoity-Toity) chases him around chairs and table; ivory fan hits bystander.
- Forister carried on pallet. Earl's carriage leaves for London with Mary, Strepp, Royale.
- O'Ruddy rides for Bath; horse lamed in puddle. Overhears Paddy reading Earl's papers aloud (a letter "Dear Sister Mary... my hand is lame from milking the cows"). Paddy and Jem robbed Earl's carriage; they took a sum of gold.
- O'Ruddy forgives them; reclaims papers.
- Bath: Jem's ballad fame; O'Ruddy announces at Earl's room. Valet mangles "O'Ruddy" to "O'Rubby."
- Earl: "The papers are in the breast of my coat." O'Ruddy threatens guests; Sir Edmund Flixton; Earl's private talk: "why didn't you read the papers?" O'Ruddy: "I would try to get a tutor."

## Ch XIII-XIV (Countess, Paddy vs. Countess)
- Earl reveals he knows of O'Ruddy's love for Mary. Earl has "Mary" come and tests him; O'Ruddy refuses table.
- Countess bursts into O'Ruddy's room, fights servants; Paddy holds her against wall with chair. O'Ruddy flees ("Bravo, Paddy!").
- Night at another inn; Paddy on ladies ("Mag Cooligan," Bantry). O'Ruddy cuffs him for mention of ladies.

## Ch XV-XVII (London)
- Paddy philosophizes on English, heathens, "Father Corrigan."
- Entry to London (bridge, fog, rain). Butcher vs brewer brawl. Shopkeeper directs them to "Pig and Turnip," Bishopsgate.
- Innkeeper: "Mr. Fullbil himself comes here at times."

## Ch XVI (mug-house, lessons)
- Mock inn-yard tale told by Jem. O'Ruddy cuffs Jem; "sticadoro proderodo sliceriscum fencing"; "My mother taught me"; "A blue one."
- O'Ruddy trains Paddy and Jem as footmen (bottle-holding lesson). Paddy and Jem gossip; Jem "befooled them."

## Ch XVIII-XIX (Fullbil's club, Red Slipper)
- Club: Fullbil (little old growling literary master), Bobbs (dramatist), Fancher (critic), Doctor Chord (little scientist), O'Ruddy's friend (unnamed). Five-minute explanation debate. "My good friend Bobbs, I see your nose gradually is turning red." Chinese kites. "Ireland... pigs at table." O'Ruddy: "Over there they don't know you are alive."
- Flixton recognizes O'Ruddy. Chord grins.
- O'Ruddy's Galway tale ("King of Galway").
- Red Slipper mug-house: Paddy and Jem with footmen posing as gentlemen; Jem sings ballad. Paddy vs. "bishop"; learned valet on bird "loriot."

## Ch XX-XXII (Kensington Gardens, Chord)
- Kensington Gardens Sunday: fashion display; mothers and daughters. Chord's gossip (Marquis of Stubblington, Lord Gram, Banellic girls, Countess Cheer).
- Mary's look back. O'Ruddy vows to marry her; Chord doubts.
- Earl's town house: walled garden, small door, oaks on lonely avenue.
- Chord: Countess once rescued by his hot rum.

## Ch XXIII-XXVI (climbing, Strammers, papers warning)
- Chord's plan; O'Ruddy climbs oak; Chord flees. Gardener Strammers with blunderbuss: "thief o' French pears." Mary takes blunderbuss: "I'm afraid it's l-l-loaded." O'Ruddy declares love; interrupted.
- Strammers's ale; Paddy and Jem befriend him; invitation for next Sunday.
- Saturday night: Chord warns of papers; suggests giving to Paddy; O'Ruddy suspects.

## Ch XXVII-XXIX (Sunday garden, Temple)
- Sunday: Paddy and Jem lured through little door; beaten by household; Earl, Countess and Chord present.
- O'Ruddy enters house; Mary locked in boudoir. He turns key; papers kicked by Mary.
- Mary: Earl's papers = title to Brede estate (Sussex) given to O'Ruddy's father; advises lawyer Josiah Brooks in Temple.
- Mary and O'Ruddy kiss. Father Donovan at St Patrick's chapel; Donovan reveals pilgrimage to Rome, ship from Rye.
- Chord visits bruised Paddy and Jem; Paddy punches Chord; Jem kicks him; Chord flees.
- Temple: Brooks; O'Ruddy's claim; Brooks's cold manner.

## Ch XXX (money, swords, departure)
- Brooks returns swords (nine, counted); O'Ruddy insists on lawsuit/compromise.
- 500 guineas from Mary via Brooks; O'Ruddy pays inn bill; tailor's new suits.
- Plans: Paddy and Jem to Rye with swords; Father Donovan to accompany.
- Early departure; Father Donovan rides with O'Ruddy.

## Ch XXXI-XXXII (Rye, Brede)
- Father Donovan's stories. Paddy attacked by nine men on Maidstone road (Paddy's head bandaged). Jem robbed the same nine (incl. Chord) of 60-70 guineas; piled their saddles.
- Rye: O'Ruddy hires nine men via Tom Peel ("Anchor" inn); pays 5 guineas each, 10 at end.
- Brede House: caretaker and wife; Sir Goddard Oxenbridge ghost (sawn in two); secret tunnel to church.
- Earl's party arrives; Strepp attacks with men; blunderbusses scatter them. Strepp refuses terms.
- Night: Strepp's men enter tunnel; O'Ruddy traps them with stones. Strepp surrenders in morning; released.
- Strepp: "King O'Ruddy."

## Ch XXXIII (Manor House, marriage)
- Paddy falls through trap-door into dungeon; freed by rope.
- Manor House conference: Earl, Countess, Mary, Strepp, Father Donovan. O'Ruddy scatters gold. Countess slaps O'Ruddy.
- Mary: "I shall marry no man whom I do not love." Countess coerces her, then Mary consents. Father Donovan blesses her.
- Married by Father Donovan. Memoirs written later with children Patrick, Mary, Terence, Kathleen, Michael, Bridget, Donovan.
